section_summary: This section records the effects of wartime exchange controls and asset freezes on Japan’s foreign payments, American residents, and private claims. Despatches from Peru describe Japanese gold shipments and yen transactions, while reports from China trace Japanese capital moving through Shanghai and Hong Kong. Later papers address yen conversion rates for repatriated Americans, Formosa, and the Japanese outlying islands.

subfiles.title: Foreign Exchange Control Ordinance, sections thirteen and fourteen
subfiles.about: Transmits the final provisions of a Japanese exchange-control ordinance.
subfiles.summary: Continued translation covers reporting identifying details for foreign-connected persons and firms, ministerial exemptions and reports, and the ordinance’s commencement.

subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy cash withdrawal
subfiles.about: Reports a Japanese Embassy check cashed for $10,000 in large bills.
subfiles.summary: The FBI recorded the serial numbers of ten $1,000 bills.

subfiles.title: Yokohama Specie Bank silver payment
subfiles.about: Reports a $154,000 bank check apparently paying for a silver shipment.
subfiles.summary: The Yokohama Specie Bank’s San Francisco branch bought a check payable through Bankers Trust in New York.

subfiles.title: Japanese diplomatic cash withdrawals
subfiles.about: Reports cash withdrawals by the Japanese Embassy and military attaché.
subfiles.summary: The FBI obtained serial numbers of the large-denomination bills.

subfiles.title: Transfer to file 894.51
subfiles.about: Records transfer of a paper to another file.
subfiles.summary: File 894.5151/257 was transferred to 894.51.

subfiles.title: Living-expense withdrawals under Japanese and U.S. freezes
subfiles.about: Considers whether to seek higher living-expense allowances for Americans in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Luthringer explains the distinction between withdrawals from U.S. bank accounts and remittances from Japan. He recounts discussions with Treasury and an interdepartmental committee, including cash limits for departing Japanese nationals. No decision was reached on approaching Japan; he recommends weighing the timing against negotiations over diplomatic expenses.

subfiles.title: Handwritten comment on living-expense issue
subfiles.about: Comments on the proposed handling of reciprocal living-expense limits.
subfiles.summary: The note appears to favor waiting until the diplomatic-expense question is settled.

subfiles.title: Proposed instruction on monthly withdrawals in Japan
subfiles.about: Drafts a reciprocal response to Japan’s 500-yen monthly withdrawal limit.
subfiles.summary: The draft would authorize warning Japan that the United States may reduce Japanese nationals’ $500 monthly allowance unless Japan raises its limit for Americans.

subfiles.title: Treatment of American residents in Japan
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram about unequal treatment under freezing orders.
subfiles.summary: References Grew’s discussion with Japan’s Foreign Office about allowances for American and Japanese residents.

subfiles.title: Japan’s shortage of foreign exchange
subfiles.about: Reports that Japan may default on maturing foreign-exchange contracts.
subfiles.summary: A source estimates Japan’s available exchange at about 20,000 reichsmarks. Allied freezes curtailed dollar, sterling, and guilder dealings; Germany reportedly restricted credits to German purchases.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Tokyo telegram on foreign exchange
subfiles.about: Restates Grew’s report on Japan’s foreign-exchange shortage.
subfiles.summary: The paraphrase repeats the reported shortage, blocked currency transactions, German demands, and Japan’s resulting difficulty meeting foreign obligations.

subfiles.title: Transmission note for Tokyo telegram
subfiles.about: Records handling of a paraphrase of Tokyo’s October 9 telegram.
subfiles.summary: An OCR-damaged note identifies the telegram and its paraphrase.

subfiles.title: Correction to Tokyo telegram
subfiles.about: Sends a correction to Grew’s October 9 telegram.
subfiles.summary: Transmits an October 12 correction to line four of the telegram’s first page.

subfiles.title: Japanese and other unusual exchange operations in Peru
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese gold imports and other Peruvian exchange transactions.
subfiles.summary: The Central Reserve Bank of Peru describes Japanese gold sold to finance Peruvian exports and supplies figures on yen trading. Norweb also reports an inactive Soviet bank account and Peru’s difficulty obtaining Swiss francs for officials in Europe, requesting U.S. guidance and cooperation.

subfiles.title: Peruvian reserve bank letter on gold transfer
subfiles.from: Banco Central de Reserva del Perú
subfiles.to: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
subfiles.about: Requests instructions for applying directly to transfer gold to Buenos Aires.
subfiles.summary: The proposed transfer would obtain Swiss francs for Peru’s diplomatic and consular expenses in Europe.

subfiles.title: Translation of Peruvian reserve bank letter
subfiles.from: Banco Central de Reserva del Perú
subfiles.to: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
subfiles.about: Translates the reserve bank’s request about a proposed gold transfer.
subfiles.summary: After Treasury declined an earlier application, the bank asks how to apply directly to move approximately $100,000 in gold to Buenos Aires for Swiss-franc credit.

subfiles.title: Sales and purchases of yen by Peruvian banks
subfiles.about: Tabulates commercial-bank yen transactions in Peru during July–September 1941.
subfiles.summary: Lists monthly sales and purchases, with swaps and cancellations deducted.

subfiles.title: German bank offer of Swiss francs in Peru
subfiles.about: Describes a German bank’s proposed route for supplying Swiss francs to Peru.
subfiles.summary: A Lima German bank offered Swiss francs through an unidentified Shanghai bank against gold deposited in Peru. The Central Reserve Bank sought U.S. comments while looking for a way to fund its European officers without objectionable banks.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Lima banking despatches
subfiles.about: Forwards two Lima despatches and requests advice on replies.
subfiles.summary: The despatches concern German, Japanese, and Swiss banking transactions in Peru.

subfiles.title: Japanese credits for mineral purchases
subfiles.from: U.S. Embassy, Lima; signed by Julian Greenup
subfiles.about: Reports Yokohama Specie Bank letters of credit for minerals from Bolivia and Chile.
subfiles.summary: A copied bank telegram describes credit for copper ore; an earlier credit covered antimony ore shipped from Chile to Japan.

subfiles.title: Handwritten Far Eastern Affairs note
subfiles.about: Contains a brief, largely illegible comment on the preceding material.
subfiles.summary: The OCR does not preserve enough text to identify the comment reliably.

subfiles.title: Request for help collecting a Japanese debt
subfiles.about: Asks how to collect $370.82 owed by a Kobe firm.
subfiles.summary: The debtor said Japanese permission was needed before it could remit payment.

subfiles.title: Reply on collection of Japanese debt
subfiles.from: Frederick Livesey for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Explains why the Department cannot presently secure payment of a Japanese debt.
subfiles.summary: Dollar payment requires Japanese authorization under exchange controls; the Department identifies no action it can take on the claimant’s behalf.

subfiles.title: Proposed release of frozen Japanese funds
subfiles.about: Points to a proposal exchanging Manchukuo yuan for release of frozen dollars.
subfiles.summary: References an offer involving 10 million yuan and $4,694,835 in frozen Japanese funds.

subfiles.title: Inquiry into Japanese capital flight through China
subfiles.from: Department of State, for Coordinator of Information
subfiles.about: Asks whether Japanese funds have moved through Chinese coastal centers.
subfiles.summary: Requests evidence and estimates for Shanghai, Tianjin, and Hong Kong.

subfiles.title: Discussion with Dr. Remer on capital-flight inquiry
subfiles.about: Records doubts that a proposed capital-flight inquiry will yield figures.
subfiles.summary: The writer recalls limited reports of Japanese capital held in Shanghai; Remer still favors sending the inquiry.

subfiles.title: Coordinator of Information request on Japanese funds
subfiles.about: Requests sources on Japanese funds leaving through Chinese centers.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum asks about Shanghai, Tianjin, Hong Kong, and the scale of any flight from the yen.

subfiles.title: Shanghai report on flight from the yen
subfiles.about: Estimates the scale and routes of Japanese capital flight through China.
subfiles.summary: Shanghai reports hundreds of millions of yen moved in 1938–40 through Chinese ports and rail routes, with far smaller flows in 1941. Its second section describes yen-note smuggling, exchange quotations, and tighter Japanese exit and export controls. It says further flight likely depended on officials’ cooperation.

subfiles.title: Hong Kong report on yen movements
subfiles.from: U.S. Consulate, Hong Kong; signed Southard
subfiles.about: Describes yen-note and credit movements through Hong Kong.
subfiles.summary: Hong Kong authorities estimated annual arrivals of about 12 million yen in notes during mid-1939 to mid-1941. The report also describes Japanese firms’ deposits and says transactions became very small after the British asset freeze.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about Japanese gold shipments
subfiles.to: Diplomatic missions in Central and South America
subfiles.about: Points to a circular request for reports on future Japanese gold shipments.
subfiles.summary: The circular sought their purpose: payment for goods or creation of exchange assets.

subfiles.title: Japanese licenses affecting U.S. establishments
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram on Japanese licenses for American official funds.
subfiles.summary: References licenses 61 and 62, described as unfreezing U.S. establishments and personnel in Japan.

subfiles.title: Company cover letter for ownership record
subfiles.about: Submits a copy of a letter documenting ownership of a Japanese company.
subfiles.summary: Requests that the enclosed ownership account be kept on file.

subfiles.title: Ownership of Sakuma Industrial Company
subfiles.about: Records The Paraffine Companies’ ownership of shares in Sakuma Industrial.
subfiles.summary: Alexander states that the American company owns 6,000 of 10,000 shares. Of those, 1,500 stand in Eikichi Sakuma’s name under documents preserving the American company’s ownership.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of company ownership record
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the Sakuma Industrial ownership papers.
subfiles.summary: Confirms that the company’s letter and enclosure will be placed in Department records.

subfiles.title: Renewed inquiry on Japanese debt claim
subfiles.about: Asks how to file a prewar debt claim after war began.
subfiles.summary: The company again cites $370.82 owed by a Kobe firm.

subfiles.title: Reply on private debt-claim procedure
subfiles.from: Green H. Hackworth for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Explains that no government procedure exists for the company’s debt claim.
subfiles.summary: The claimant may need to pursue ordinary private collection when conditions permit.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about August 1942 yen-dollar exchange rate
subfiles.about: Seeks an exchange rate for settling a repatriated employee’s salary claim.
subfiles.summary: The attorney compares the 3⅓-yen rate used during repatriation with a different rate on the subsidiary’s 1941 balance sheet and asks for a reliable August 31, 1942 rate.

subfiles.title: Reply on wartime yen valuation
subfiles.about: Explains limitations of the repatriation exchange rate.
subfiles.summary: The rate was negotiated and did not establish the yen’s market value; the draft suggests consulting financial institutions.

subfiles.title: Accounts Division memorandum on yen rates
subfiles.about: Supplies exchange-rate evidence for answering the United Artists inquiry.
subfiles.summary: The division cites a Swiss Legation note and its own 4.235-yen settlement rate, while lacking grounds to explain the 3⅓-yen repatriation rate.

subfiles.title: Swiss Legation exchange-rate note
subfiles.about: States reported official yen, Swiss-franc, and dollar parities.
subfiles.summary: The copied note gives a calculated parity of 4.235 yen per dollar.

subfiles.title: Navy instruction on a two-yen dollar rate
subfiles.about: Sets a military exchange rate of two yen per dollar.
subfiles.summary: The instruction applies the rate to all yen issues in that area without setting a precedent elsewhere.

subfiles.title: Conversation on Swiss purchases of yen
subfiles.about: Records information on yen and Swiss-franc conversion.
subfiles.summary: Mitchell reports a September 1943 Manila quotation and a Swiss-franc dollar parity.

subfiles.title: Referral of Frank Fesperman yen inquiry
subfiles.to: State Department, Special War Problems Division
subfiles.about: Refers a request to exchange Japanese yen for U.S. currency.
subfiles.summary: Treasury forwards Fesperman’s letter and receipt for State Department reply.

subfiles.title: Interest on Japanese foreign securities
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram on interest payments for Japanese securities.
subfiles.summary: References a Berlin announcement concerning Japanese dollar and sterling securities.

subfiles.title: Cover memorandum on exchange rates in Formosa and islands
subfiles.about: Forwards papers on military yen rates for Formosa and outlying islands.
subfiles.summary: The papers were intended for a meeting with Mr. Bell; originals went to Mr. Grew.

subfiles.title: Impasse over yen exchange rate
subfiles.to: Mr. Ballantine; Mr. Dumm; Mr. Clayton; Mr. Grew
subfiles.about: Seeks a high-level decision on the military yen rate for Formosa and outlying islands.
subfiles.summary: Treasury favors five cents per yen, while State favors ten cents in Formosa. Because the rates in both areas must align, Collado proposes discussion with Secretary Morgenthau and, if needed, presidential settlement.

subfiles.title: State Department case for a ten-cent yen rate
subfiles.from: Division of Financial and Monetary Affairs
subfiles.about: Argues for a ten-cent initial yen rate in Formosa and Japanese outlying islands.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum says a five-cent rate could worsen inflation in Formosa and create political and economic difficulties for its Chinese population and neighboring territories. State accepts a low rate in some islands only if it does not determine Formosa’s rate.

subfiles.title: Japanese parity for yen, peso, and baht
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese authorities’ currency parity announcement.
subfiles.summary: A Swiss report says the yen, Philippine peso, and Thai baht were set at parity.

subfiles.title: Request for Japan’s 1940 exchange regulations
subfiles.from: Sanford D. Beecher, Duane, Morris & Heckscher
subfiles.about: Requests Japanese exchange-control law and regulations applicable in 1940.
subfiles.summary: The documents are sought for John B. Geary’s income-tax matter; a 1941 published translation does not cover the relevant year.

subfiles.title: Reply on unavailable Japanese regulations
subfiles.from: Erle A. Dickover for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Responds to the request for Japan’s 1940 exchange law.
subfiles.summary: The Department says it lacks copies and knows of no government source able to supply them.

subfiles.title: Exchange-rate memorandum reference
subfiles.about: Points to a memorandum on yen rates for Formosa and outlying islands.
subfiles.summary: Records the related memorandum’s date and file location.

subfiles.title: Fiscal Planning Committee meeting reference
subfiles.about: Points to a committee memorandum discussing the exchange rate.
subfiles.summary: Records the meeting memorandum’s date and file location.

subfiles.title: Proposed directives for Japanese outlying islands
subfiles.from: Captain L. S. Sabin, Navy Department
subfiles.about: Requests State Department comment on proposed island-government directives.
subfiles.summary: The financial directive leaves the yen rate blank pending interdepartmental discussions; Sabin also requests formal concurrence in the political directive.

subfiles.title: State concurrence in political directive
subfiles.about: Conveys State Department concurrence in a political directive for the islands.
subfiles.summary: Comments on the financial directive and accounting guide are promised later.

subfiles.title: Enclosure charge slip
subfiles.about: Records internal movement of an enclosure.
subfiles.summary: The charge-slip entries are mostly illegible.

subfiles.title: DCR transfer sheet
subfiles.about: Records transfer of one enclosure to a confidential file.
subfiles.summary: The sheet identifies a file number and a confidential-file destination.
